overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair has discretion over who speaks, and limiting public comment to in-person attendees is not a violation, though public participation is encouraged.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not let individuals who attended the August 15 meeting virtually participate, including a co-chair of a building committee who was denied speaking time.
allegations.key_passage: Because it is within the Chair’s discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, he did not violate the Open Meeting Law by restricting individuals from speaking during the August 15 meeting even though those individuals may be members of, or acting as representatives of, other town boards or committees.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's practice of allowing public comment only from people attending in person, not virtually, violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, the allegation that the Board only allowed public comment by those individuals who attended meetings in person would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.
